text:
Morgan: Quick Q — onboarding run for the new vectorizer is spitting debug lines with emails. example grep output:
```
2026-01-07T13:02:11Z INFO batch_process user_email=alice@example.com input_len=512
```
Are we allowed to keep those in staging logs for troubleshooting?
Sarah: Short answer: no. Email is PII (class 2). Don't log raw emails. Use hashed or tokenized IDs. Staging doesn't change classification.
Raj: If we rotate/TTL logs after 24h and only expose to a small SRE group, is that an exception?
Sarah: Rotation helps but doesn't make it OK. There is an exception path: file a temporary access approval w/ retention + scope. @eng-security-bot can open that for you.
eng-security-bot: SEC ticket created: SEC-1743 — temporary access request for `redactor-staging` logs. Requester: Morgan. TTL: 48h. Link: https://internal/SEC-1743
Morgan: Thanks — I'll scrub the logging code and push a PR with masked fields. Plan: replace `user_email` with `user_id` and add `LOG_REDACTION=true` flag.
Raj: Also ensure embeddings/outputs don't contain full prompts. We had a regression earlier where prompt text leaked. Add unit test that asserts `user_email` not in logs during CI.
Sarah: +1. Include a migration note in the PR explaining the incident class and the required follow-ups (SEC ticket close, audit). Use config name `REDWOOD_LOG_REDACTION` so it's obvious.
Olivia: I can approve short-lived staging access once the SEC ticket is up. Morgan, please DM me the ticket link when you have PR.
Morgan: Will do. I'll also update the runbook snippet and paste it in the PR. :thumbsup:
Sarah: One more thing — avoid sending raw emails to external vendors in logs (S3/stackdriver). If you must, use tokenization and a mapping table stored in KMS-protected DB.
Morgan: Got it, thanks all. I'll handle PR and close SEC-1743 when done.
